Can you confirm if there are any ongoing maintenance windows or known capacity issues on your side? This is blocking usage for a handful of paying customers.

Please treat as P1.

Thanks,
Alex Turner

Subject: Re: Production 5xx spike — experiencing timeouts and 429s

Quick status update (triage):
- Observed: Dedicated pool ‘wd-dedicated-13’ shows a sharp queue backlog starting 08:48 PDT. Autoscaler telemetry indicates several allocation attempts failed with "insufficient capacity" errors for a 40s window.
- Contributing factor: GC on a long-running serving process caused node reclamation delays; autoscaler did not bring nodes fully online before traffic ramp.
- Action taken (09:28): manual add of 4 gpus to the Dedicated pool; enabled temporary routing to fallback Hosted pool with quantized model variant (lower throughput but faster startup).
- Impact: error rate down ~70% in the first 10 min; some 429s persist due to client-side retry storms. Recommend advising customers to increase exponential backoff and applying token-bucket rate limiter at their side.

Open items:
- SUP-2345 created to track root cause and prevent autoscaler cold-start race (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-2345).
- Need sign-off to proactively increase min-instances for this tenant to avoid future cold starts.

I will push a timeline and postmortem draft after we stabilize.

— Rishi
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Note: attaching quick SLO snapshot (slo_latency_chart_20270518.png)

Alex —

Thank you for the quick report and for the logs. We pushed a manual scale to your Dedicated pool and activated a temporary routing rule to the Hosted fallback pool (quantized variant) at 09:28 PDT. You should see reduced 5xxs; we are observing a ~70% reduction in errors. A few 429s persist as we see client retries crowding remaining capacity.

What we did:
- Manual +4 GPUs to dedicate capacity
- Enabled fallback routing to Hosted quantized model variant
- Created SUP-2345 to track root cause and fix autoscaler startup race

Immediate ask on your side: if you can momentarily increase retry backoff (recommended: base 200ms, multiplier 2.0, max 5s) and add a small jitter, that will reduce retry amplification while we finish stabilization.

Next steps: Rishi will prepare a postmortem and proposed config change to min-instances. We'll share it by end of day. Marissa will coordinate the credits conversation if necessary.

Appreciate your patience — we are treating this as priority.

— Stephanie
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
